s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive hyperpigmented skin lesion with irregular borders and variable coloration, presenting with satellite lesions and areas of regression
salient_findings: Irregular brown-black patch on the left lateral ankle
Confluent mottled black and brown macules with satellite lesions
Areas of regression within the lesion
key_facts: The patient initially developed the lesion at age 6
The lesion measured 3.6 × 3 cm at initial presentation
The lesion grew progressively, measuring 5.5 × 5-cm at age 9
Two discrete areas of regression were noted at age 12
Dermoscopy showed discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas
Histopathology at age 9 showed a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes
Histopathology at age 12 showed atypical nevus with areas of dermal fibrosis
Gene Expression Testing score was -7.1, consistent with a benign nevus

shortlist.label: Congenital Melanocytic Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: matches the description of a progressive hyperpigmented skin lesion with irregular borders and satellite lesions

shortlist.label: Atypical Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: histopathology at age 9 and 12 showed features consistent with an atypical nevus

shortlist.label: Dysplastic Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: presence of large nested melanocytes and random atypia on histopathology

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: cannot be entirely ruled out despite benign gene expression testing score, due to the presence of atypical features and regression

shortlist.label: Pigmented Spindle Cell Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: dermoscopic features of discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient developed the lesion at age 6, which is consistent with a congenital melanocytic nevus that may not be apparent at birth but becomes visible later in childhood. The lesion's progressive growth, irregular shape, and presence of satellite lesions also support this diagnosis. The histopathology and gene expression testing results are consistent with a benign nevus, which further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Atypical Nevus
rejected.why: While the histopathology showed atypical features, the gene expression testing score was consistent with a benign nevus, making atypical nevus less likely.

rejected.label: Dysplastic Nevus
rejected.why: Dysplastic nevi are typically smaller and more uniform in color, which does not match the patient's lesion.

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: The gene expression testing score and histopathology results do not support a diagnosis of melanoma.

rejected.label: Pigmented Spindle Cell Nevus
rejected.why: The patient's lesion does not have the characteristic spindle cell morphology of a pigmented spindle cell nevus.
